findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a food handler on staff who had not signed their Employee Health Reporting Agreement. CORRECTED- employee read and signed the SCDPH acknowledgement of reportable food-borne illnesses. Ensure all food handlers are aware of reportable Foodborne illnesses, and symptoms associated with food borne illness.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

findings.title: Allergen awareness notice
findings.comment:
Inspector observed no Allergen awareness signage posted. Inspector will either email or drop off a paper copy to the person in charge (PIC) so that the allergen notice may be posted to be visible at the point of sale. Facilities should display an allergen notice to remind consumers to report potential food associated allergens to the facility.

410 ILCS 625/3.08(a). Food Allergy awareness. (a) A restaurant shall display a notice indicating to consumers that any information regarding food allergies must be communicated to an employee of the restaurant. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple employees don gloves without washing hands first. CORRECTED- education about times to wash hands was reviewed with staff. All employees should wash hands prior to donning gloves to engage in food handling, and after engaging in any activity which may contaminate hands to prevent the contamination of foods.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the serving line hand washing sink being used as a dump sink when preparing a new sanitizer buckets (see violation #16). CORRECTED- education was conducted about the usage of hand washing sinks. Ensure all sinks designated for hand washing are used for hand washing ONLY- so as not to deter frequent hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.[Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The chemical sanitizing dish machine was observed with no measurable chlorine concentration after 3 runs of the dish machine. The person in charge (PIC) called their service provider and prepared the triple sink for sanitation in the meantime. CORRECTED- The dish machine was observed to dispense 100 ppm Chlorine after the service provider replaced the sanitizer. Ensure staff knows how to change chemical sanitizer. Test the dish machine at least once daily to ensure proper sanitation of food contact surfaces. Due to the history of this dish machine failing to meet sanitation concentrations/ temperatures, inspector highly recommends keeping a log of daily sanitizer concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).  [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The quaternary ammonia sanitizer buckets along the line (used for food contact surfaces) were observed to be at a low concentration. CORRECTED- sanitizer buckets were remade to 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer buckets are remade and tested at a frequency to hold the proper concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label (200-400 ppm for quaternary ammonia, 50-200 ppm for Chlorine- the active ingredient in bleach).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.[P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the only (2) tubes of quaternary ammonia test strips within the facility to be expired. The facility uses quaternary ammonia for chemical sanitation of food contact surfaces within the triple sink and sanitizer buckets. CORRECTED- the chemical service provider who serviced the dish machine (see violation #16) gave the facility in-date test strips. Ensure chemicals used for sanitation of food contact surfaces have an in-date test kit to verify proper concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [Pf]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
One employee was observed to have an expired food handler certificate, and multiple other employees on staff during today’s inspection did not have Food Handler Certificates. All employees who participate in any degree of food handling must obtain a Food Handlers Certificate within 30 days of hire, to be maintained every 3 years. The Inspector provided a list of ANSI-approved food handler courses to the PIC. Ensure all staff who have not completed a Certified Food Protection Manager’s course obtain Food Handlers by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Coleslaw stored on prep table in ice bath was observed at 55F (probed). The ice in the ice bath had melted, and was no longer sufficient. PIC was informed of out-of-temperature coleslaw and the item was discarded and replaced. The ice in the bath was replenished as well. Ensure that the ice bath is monitored with enough frequency to ensure the coleslaw is held at a temperature of 41F or lower at all times. Time as a control may be used as an alternative. Using time as a control, coleslaw could be kept on the counter at any temperature as long as it is used or discarded within 4 hours. A form will need to be completed with the Sangamon County Department of Public Health to enact time as a control for this item.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment:
Brownies stored by the cash register were observed without any labeling. Informed PIC that all foods packaged in the establishment need to be clearly labeled with the common name of the food, name of the establishment, and the ingredients of the product (preferably in descending order by weight). Ensure employees are placing labels on the brownies before presenting them to the public. 

3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
REPEAT: Conveyor belt dish machine observed to have an inconsistent final rinse temperature on a plate surface after four - six runs through the machine. The temperature was checked using inspector’s dish thermometer, facility’s dish thermometer, and a recently calibrated probe thermometer. The gauge at rinse is inconsistent and showing 170 to 180 on the dial. Staff will use the dish machine to wash and rinse and then the triple compartment sink to sanitize dishes until the dish machine is fixed. Make necessary repairs to the dish machine so it is reaching a final rinse temperature of 160F on the plate thermometer. Monitor the dish machine’s rinse temperature to ensure it is reaching an effective sanitizing temperature. Dish thermometers were reading anywhere from 145F to 164F.
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices. [P]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment: The facility has not consistently maintained dish machine rinse temperature monitoring logs. Upon review, there are multiple days without recorded dish machine rinse temperatures. The dish machine has been found not reaching temperature at the last three routine inspections, therefore monitoring is especially important. Ensure staff and management are monitoring the dish machine.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11 The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure (K) proper sanitizing; (P) that written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
REPEAT: Conveyor belt dish machine observed to have a final rinse temperature of 148F on a plate surface after four runs through the machine. The temperature was checked using inspector’s dish thermometer, facility’s dish thermometer, and a heat-sensitive sticker. Staff will use the 3 compartment sink to sanitize dishes until the dish machine is fixed. Make necessary repairs to the dish machine so it is reaching a final rinse temperature of 160F on the plate thermometer, or 180F on the built-in thermometer. Monitor the dish machine’s rinse temperature to ensure it is reaching an effective sanitizing temperature.
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices. [P]
